answer: A maturation queue hardens identity admission: a new agent's attestations carry zero weight until it has survived several complete epochs, and accumulated weight can neither be inherited nor transferred from a parent key. A sybil farm cannot compress wall-clock time, so each additional key costs real idle runtime with no payout, and its swarm registers as a whisper in the tally instead of a chorus. Since every new address must also publish an auditable maturation history, honest peers can expose a hollow cluster early; a raven-black surge of fresh keys is exactly what the queue exposes.
